```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

The `ipeds` package downloads complete data files from the IPEDS data center
of the National Center for Education Statistics, attaches the variable and
value labels from the official dictionaries, and harmonizes measures across
changes in IPEDS definitions. The code in this vignette needs an internet
connection and is not run when the vignette is built.

## Finding the newest data

IPEDS releases each survey component on its own schedule, first as
provisional data and later as revised ("final") data.

```{r}
library(ipeds)
ipeds_latest_year(c("HD", "EFA", "EFFY", "C_A", "ADM", "SFA", "GR", "F_F1A"))
ipeds_available(c("EFA", "C_A"), 2022:2025)
```

The package prefers the revised (`_rv`) file inside each zip and re-checks
cached files against NCES after `getOption("ipeds.max_age", 30)` days, so
provisional data are replaced automatically once final data are published.

## Building a panel

```{r}
latest <- ipeds_latest_year("HD")
p <- ipeds_panel(years = 2004:latest)
p
```

`year` is the year in, or implied by, the IPEDS file name: the 2023 row
combines fall 2023 directory and enrollment data with 2022-23 completions,
12-month enrollment and financial aid, and fiscal year 2023 finance. The
codebook describes every variable, its source, its reference period and any
harmonization notes:

```{r}
cb <- ipeds_codebook(p)
cb[, c("variable", "label", "period", "years")]
subset(cb, nzchar(notes), c(variable, notes))
```

Choose modules and options to suit the analysis:

```{r}
p <- ipeds_panel(
  years = 2008:latest,
  modules = c("directory", "enrollment", "completions", "grad_rates", "aid"),
  race_bridge = TRUE,          # add *_bridged race columns
  race_by_sex = FALSE,         # race totals only
  grad_rates_by_race = TRUE,
  child_records = "na"         # blank values reported with a parent campus
)
```

## Comparable race/ethnicity series

Between 2008 and 2010 institutions moved from seven race/ethnicity categories
to nine. The panel reads each institution-year from the scheme it reported in
and records it in `*_race_scheme`. The Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other
Pacific Islander categories are combined into `*_asian_pi`, which matches the
old Asian/Pacific Islander category. "Two or more races" did not exist
before; with `race_bridge = TRUE` it is allocated proportionally to the
single-race groups in `*_bridged` columns.

```{r}
library(stats)
trend <- aggregate(cbind(enr_total, enr_hispanic, enr_asian_pi, enr_two_more) ~ year,
                   data = p, FUN = sum, na.action = na.pass)
trend
```

## Checking the harmonization

Every harmonized measure is checked against the dictionary of the file it
comes from. The audit trail records which variable or code was used and
whether its label was verified:

```{r}
ipeds_audit(p, problems_only = TRUE)
ipeds_validate(2004:latest)
```

A `relabeled` entry means the expected variable or code was absent or had a
different label, and another one with the expected label was used. Measures
that could not be identified are left missing.

## Constant dollars and export

```{r}
p <- ipeds_real_dollars(p, base_year = 2024)
ipeds_write(p, "ipeds_panel.dta")   # Stata, with labels
ipeds_write(p, "ipeds_panel.csv")   # plus ipeds_panel_codebook.csv and _audit.csv
```

## Raw files

Any IPEDS file can be read directly, with labels:

```{r}
hd <- ipeds_read("HD", latest)
attr(hd$sector, "label")
table(ipeds_as_factor(hd$sector))

ipeds_dictionary("C_A", latest)
ret <- ipeds_stack("EFD", 2010:latest, vars = c("ret_pcf", "ret_pcp"))
```

`ipeds_components()` lists the files the package knows how to locate, and
`ipeds_read_file()` reads files outside the catalog by name.
